title: The Insiders Podcast: Jalen Hurts OUT for season (lung blood clots) + Josh Jacobs removed from exempt list
text: 0:00:10.039 --> 0:00:13.280 The NFL's fall meeting is underway, bringing the Eagles' handling 0:00:13.320 --> 0:00:16.730 of Jalen Hurts' blood clots into focus, plus some positive 0:00:16.790 --> 0:00:19.610 signs for two injured quarterbacks looking to get back on 0:00:19.670 --> 0:00:20.209 the field. 0:00:20.450 --> 0:00:21.130 And we know B. 0:00:21.170 --> 0:00:24.070 Sean Robinson's impact on the field. Today, you learn more 0:00:24.090 --> 0:00:27.340 about it off the field as the NFL's Scrimmage Arts 0:00:27.660 --> 0:00:30.300 leader joins the show live. 0:00:30.360 --> 0:00:30.940 Welcome, everybody. 0:00:30.960 --> 0:00:33.600 Great to be here with you for the Insiders presented 0:00:33.620 --> 0:00:37.809 by Progressive Insurance. From the league meeting, Ian Rappaport, Mike Garofalo, 0:00:37.870 --> 0:00:41.170 Judy Batista, with Jeff Darlington along with us as well. Guys, 0:00:41.409 --> 0:00:43.570 let's begin with the biggest headline, of course, and that 0:00:43.630 --> 0:00:47.030 is still Jalen Hurts in the Philadelphia Eagles. Quarterback is 0:00:47.090 --> 0:00:49.160 expected to miss the remainder of the season after blood 0:00:49.170 --> 0:00:50.640 clots were found in his lungs. 0:00:50.740 --> 0:00:52.279 As all of the events and. 0:00:52.260 --> 0:00:56.460 Details preceding that discovery show, continue to come under scrutiny. 0:00:56.500 --> 0:00:59.160 And today at the NFL Fall League meeting kind of 0:00:59.180 --> 0:01:01.420 provided the backdrop for the latest on how the Hurts 0:01:01.460 --> 0:01:05.350 situation was handled. NFL Chief Medical Officer Dr. Alan Sills 0:01:05.770 --> 0:01:09.030 with a staunch defense of the Eagles and medical professionals 0:01:09.190 --> 0:01:10.550 involved in Hurts' care. 0:01:11.069 --> 0:01:15.030 Our first obligation as team physicians is always and evermore 0:01:15.069 --> 0:01:15.910 will be to the patient. 0:01:16.650 --> 0:01:17.610 It's to do the right thing. 0:01:17.870 --> 0:01:18.110 Why? 0:01:18.150 --> 0:01:20.380 Because that's what we're licensed to do. That's our standard 0:01:20.400 --> 0:01:23.190 of care That's the standard we're held to. That's the 0:01:23.209 --> 0:01:25.370 standard we're licensed to. That's the oath that we've pledged. 0:01:26.450 --> 0:01:27.310 And that's what happens. 0:01:27.390 --> 0:01:30.450 And so any idea or any suggestion that a team 0:01:30.510 --> 0:01:34.110 physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a general manager, 0:01:34.130 --> 0:01:37.330 a team owner, it just doesn't happen. I can't speak 0:01:37.360 --> 0:01:39.500 to what happened in the dark ages when Jeff started 0:01:39.540 --> 0:01:42.080 working for the league, but I can tell you in 0:01:42.140 --> 0:01:44.919 my 30 years in sports medicine and today, there is 0:01:45.080 --> 0:01:49.670 no doctor who is taking orders from me. a football person, 0:01:49.890 --> 0:01:54.970 a non-medical person, period. And, very importantly, today in medicine 0:01:54.990 --> 0:01:57.590 we're all about shared decision making. You know, if any 0:01:57.670 --> 0:01:59.070 one of you comes and sits with me in my 0:01:59.130 --> 0:02:01.640 office and we talk about your situation, I'm going to 0:02:01.680 --> 0:02:04.120 give you the data, the facts, and my opinion, but 0:02:04.160 --> 0:02:06.300 ultimately we're going to make a shared decision together in 0:02:06.340 --> 0:02:09.000 which your voice as the patient really matters. The notion 0:02:09.020 --> 0:02:11.540 that there are external factors or that any of our 0:02:11.590 --> 0:02:14.929 physicians would put a player in harm's way, that's nonsense. 0:02:16.470 --> 0:02:19.350 And I think also anybody who is not sitting in 0:02:19.389 --> 0:02:22.480 that room, if you're not sitting in that room with 0:02:22.560 --> 0:02:25.840 that patient and you don't have all the data, if 0:02:25.880 --> 0:02:28.160 you are speculating as a physician on what should have 0:02:28.180 --> 0:02:31.160 been done, you are unprofessional and unethical in doing that. 0:02:31.380 --> 0:02:32.940 I'll just sum it up by saying that I have 0:02:33.000 --> 0:02:35.540 complete confidence in the Eagles medical staff and their handling 0:02:35.590 --> 0:02:38.490 of this situation, and I would characterize their work as 0:02:38.669 --> 0:02:43.750 very conservative, very patient-focused, and appropriately guarded at every step. 0:02:44.139 --> 0:02:46.720 Okay, let's get right to it. Ian, let's start right there. 0:02:47.100 --> 0:02:49.450 After hearing what Dr. Sills had to say about how 0:02:49.470 --> 0:02:51.610 the Eagles have handled this situation, how does that meet 0:02:51.650 --> 0:02:54.800 your understanding of what's gone on throughout this process? 0:02:56.470 --> 0:03:00.050 A very fiery Alan Sills, probably as passionate as really 0:03:00.110 --> 0:03:02.510 we have ever heard him, taking so many of the 0:03:02.570 --> 0:03:04.880 things that we've talked about publicly to heart. 0:03:04.910 --> 0:03:07.620 Now, let's obviously talk about the Jalen Hurts situation. 0:03:07.660 --> 0:03:09.600 We got a little bit of a tick-tock here as 0:03:09.639 --> 0:03:13.460 far as how this happened, what treatment he received, and when. 0:03:13.520 --> 0:03:14.620 So Hurts essentially. 0:03:15.070 --> 0:03:18.550 in London, was taken to the Cleveland Clinic in consultation 0:03:18.610 --> 0:03:20.850 with the NFL. And the NFL actually has been in 0:03:20.960 --> 0:03:24.040 lockstep with the Philadelphia Eagles in all of this situation, 0:03:24.060 --> 0:03:27.679 which is why the NFL, believing the Eagles handled this 0:03:27.720 --> 0:03:29.160 the right way and saying there's going to be no 0:03:29.240 --> 0:03:33.470 consequences for Philadelphia, makes sense because everything they did, guys, 0:03:33.780 --> 0:03:36.730 was while working with the Philadelphia Eagles. So anyway, Hurts 0:03:36.770 --> 0:03:40.390 went to the The clinic, he received tests. They cleared 0:03:40.430 --> 0:03:42.710 him to be on the field, which is the most 0:03:42.790 --> 0:03:46.590 important football part of this. He ended up playing. He 0:03:46.690 --> 0:03:50.680 reported that his calf got cleated, which is how they 0:03:50.720 --> 0:03:53.619 believe the superficial blood clot turned into a deep vein 0:03:53.660 --> 0:03:57.560 thrombosis blood clot, traveled from his calf to his lungs, 0:03:58.040 --> 0:04:02.110 which was then revealed, Mike, in the ultrasound on Wednesday. 0:04:02.670 --> 0:04:04.850 which is what led to the realization that he had 0:04:05.250 --> 0:04:08.790 not one blood clot, but then multiple blood clots, eventually. 0:04:08.370 --> 0:04:09.330 Landing on IR. 0:04:09.670 --> 0:04:13.170 Here's the football facts that we know. Jalen Hurts is 0:04:13.210 --> 0:04:16.130 not expected to play this season as he undergoes three 0:04:16.190 --> 0:04:20.770 months of blood thinners. Everything else, all of the other discussions, 0:04:21.810 --> 0:04:24.440 is no doubt something that the public and the NFL 0:04:24.480 --> 0:04:25.860 world is going to keep talking about. 0:04:26.000 --> 0:04:27.560 Some have speculated career ending. 0:04:27.640 --> 0:04:29.900 We have heard nothing to that end, and the expectation 0:04:29.920 --> 0:04:31.480 is that Jalen Hurts is going to come back from this. 0:04:32.450 --> 0:04:36.530 We have reported extensively on players previously who had blood 0:04:36.589 --> 0:04:38.430 clots that then had to go on blood thinners and 0:04:38.450 --> 0:04:42.470 then were taken from action for months on end. So 0:04:42.910 --> 0:04:45.510 I think this is the first time for the general 0:04:45.690 --> 0:04:48.140 NFL consuming public and NFL reporting public. 0:04:48.160 --> 0:04:49.620 I'm raising my hand. You can't see me right now. 0:04:50.339 --> 0:04:52.720 That didn't know the difference between a superficial blood clot 0:04:53.020 --> 0:04:55.779 and deep vein thrombosis. So a lot of the questions 0:04:55.800 --> 0:04:58.580 have been, how did they clear him to play with 0:04:58.640 --> 0:05:00.420 a blood clot in the first place? Now, I did 0:05:00.520 --> 0:05:02.870 ask Alan Sills about that today, and I said, a 0:05:02.940 --> 0:05:06.750 superficial blood clot, is that a common occurrence? when it 0:05:06.770 --> 0:05:09.410 comes to NFL players and clearing them to play through that. 0:05:09.610 --> 0:05:12.969 Is that the normal course of action? He would not 0:05:13.029 --> 0:05:15.469 answer that, Judy, because he said there are a lot 0:05:15.510 --> 0:05:16.290 of factors that go. 0:05:16.210 --> 0:05:17.810 Into it and it's a case-by-case basis. 0:05:17.830 --> 0:05:19.950 He said, I'm not trying to dodge your question, but 0:05:20.680 --> 0:05:22.940 he also noted the risk for the players involved and 0:05:22.960 --> 0:05:26.000 that you have this conversation with a player beforehand as 0:05:26.060 --> 0:05:29.060 well because the player has the ability to say whether 0:05:29.080 --> 0:05:31.760 he wants to play or not play as well. I 0:05:31.980 --> 0:05:33.860 have talked to doctors over the past couple of days 0:05:33.900 --> 0:05:37.150 and said, theoretically, if he came across a superficial blood clot, 0:05:37.190 --> 0:05:40.650 would you clear a player to play? They kind of 0:05:40.670 --> 0:05:43.810 like Sills. And in the end said, yeah, I probably would. 0:05:43.910 --> 0:05:47.010 So the Eagles believe that they did everything according to 0:05:47.850 --> 0:05:48.729 the way that they should have. 0:05:49.110 --> 0:05:51.039 And Alan Sills in the NFL believe that as well. 0:05:51.510 --> 0:05:53.950 First of all, let me reiterate, that was as angry 0:05:54.070 --> 0:05:56.669 as I have ever heard Alan Sills sound. I mean, 0:05:56.710 --> 0:05:59.600 he was angry at the coverage, at the questioning of 0:05:59.620 --> 0:06:01.820 the medical— of the ethics of the medical team. 0:06:02.620 --> 0:06:03.720 A few things stood out to me. 0:06:03.880 --> 0:06:05.720 He emphasized multiple. 0:06:05.300 --> 0:06:12.210 Times patient autonomy, patient autonomy. The patient— ultimately. 0:06:10.700 --> 0:06:11.850 His wishes prevail. 0:06:12.390 --> 0:06:14.950 The doctors, the medical team could certainly have pulled him 0:06:15.110 --> 0:06:16.990 off the field if they thought it was dangerous. They 0:06:17.050 --> 0:06:19.609 obviously did not think it was dangerous. They presented the 0:06:19.670 --> 0:06:24.120 information correctly. to Jalen Hurts and to the team. Jalen Hurts, 0:06:24.240 --> 0:06:26.960 if he had concerns, could have pulled himself out of 0:06:26.980 --> 0:06:30.729 the game. Now, that's probably unrealistic for a quarterback in 0:06:30.750 --> 0:06:34.930 the NFL. And ultimately, the Eagles, if they were concerned 0:06:35.130 --> 0:06:38.250 about his safety, could have said, we're sitting him down. 0:06:39.120 --> 0:06:41.299 None of them came to that conclusion, and. 0:06:41.240 --> 0:06:44.380 He played— my conclusion from all of this, from the last 0:06:44.400 --> 0:06:48.339 few days, is this has been a messaging disaster. If 0:06:48.839 --> 0:06:52.979 you believe everybody's account that the Eagles doctors and the 0:06:53.060 --> 0:06:57.460 independent doctors behaved appropriately, why they did not put out 0:06:57.520 --> 0:07:01.659 that timeline yesterday or when they pulled him off the field, 0:07:01.720 --> 0:07:04.039 when they said that he was going to be treated 0:07:04.080 --> 0:07:06.560 for blood clots and was not going to play, why 0:07:06.670 --> 0:07:10.350 they didn't put— somebody with respect to Nick Sirianni, somebody 0:07:10.550 --> 0:07:14.730 other than Nick Sirianni, who was fully briefed and knew 0:07:14.770 --> 0:07:17.680 the TikTok, why they didn't put that person out there 0:07:17.710 --> 0:07:20.420 to answer the questions, why they still haven't put anybody 0:07:20.500 --> 0:07:23.380 out there other than Dr. Alan Sills to answer the questions, 0:07:23.540 --> 0:07:27.060 I don't understand. But that exacerbated what was already a 0:07:27.170 --> 0:07:31.670 very confusing and scary situation It never needed to get 0:07:31.750 --> 0:07:33.090 to the level that it reached. 0:07:33.530 --> 0:07:33.850 All right. 0:07:33.910 --> 0:07:37.510 There has been other activity here at the league meetings. 0:07:37.590 --> 0:07:40.190 Peter O'Reilly, who is the league executive in charge of 0:07:40.230 --> 0:07:43.810 international games, said today that he expects that the league 0:07:44.010 --> 0:07:48.240 might play 10 international games. Next season, they are playing 0:07:48.500 --> 0:07:51.460 nine this season. They have loved what they've gotten out 0:07:51.500 --> 0:07:54.640 of it, the fan reaction, the ratings in those countries. 0:07:55.300 --> 0:07:57.840 Ten is the maximum that they are allowed to play 0:07:57.940 --> 0:08:00.610 under the current CBA, so they do not need to 0:08:00.650 --> 0:08:04.370 get permission from the Players' Union to go further. Other 0:08:04.450 --> 0:08:08.550 things that came to light was— Penalties are up. Offensive 0:08:08.610 --> 0:08:11.770 holding penalties are the thing that is way up. And 0:08:11.860 --> 0:08:14.600 Troy Vincent, who is in charge of football ops here, 0:08:14.900 --> 0:08:17.280 said they really want to tell the officials, stop calling 0:08:17.320 --> 0:08:20.140 it when it is away from the play. And as 0:08:20.200 --> 0:08:22.750 a result, probably, of penalties being up, time of game 0:08:22.950 --> 0:08:25.770 is also up by three minutes, which the league generally 0:08:25.810 --> 0:08:26.390 does not like. 0:08:27.110 --> 0:08:28.630 This is also a time we get to talk to 0:08:29.130 --> 0:08:31.190 owners as they come through here, maybe some owners who 0:08:31.210 --> 0:08:33.819 have some football situations that we would like to know 0:08:33.860 --> 0:08:35.839 more about, the commanders, the Colts. 0:08:36.100 --> 0:08:37.260 We tried.
